The person comes first.

A useful care plan starts with the person’s routine, their preferences, and the people around them.

Respect the familiar.

Everyday routines and personal choices matter. Discuss where support would help and where independence should be protected.

Keep the family involved.

Agree how updates will be shared, who to contact, and how questions or concerns will be handled.

Make responsibilities clear.

Understand who will provide support, what each visit includes, and how the plan will be reviewed as needs change.

A clearer way to begin.

Three conversations that help turn an unfamiliar decision into a practical plan.

  1. 1

    Describe what’s needed.

    Consider everyday routines, the kind of help needed, and any recommendations from the treating clinician.

  2. 2

    Understand the options.

    Discuss the service area, professional qualifications, timing, costs and the scope of care.

  3. 3

    Agree on the care.

    Set clear expectations for the routine, family updates and reviewing support as needs change.

Questions families ask.

A few practical details to help you prepare.

How do I know which care service to explore?

Start with daily needs and the treating clinician’s recommendations. Nursing, physiotherapy and everyday assistance have different roles. A clinical assessment may be needed to determine the appropriate support.

Can I plan support before hospital discharge?

Planning ahead allows time to discuss discharge advice, the home environment, equipment if needed, and service availability. Confirm the plan with the treating team before making arrangements.

What should be included in a care quote?

Ask about the service, visit or shift length, tasks included, caregiver role and any additional charges. Confirm payment and cancellation terms before arranging care.

Where is care available?

The service area and local availability need to be confirmed directly with Gentle Hands before arranging care. Contact details are still being finalised for this homepage preview.
